jobs.description:
**Company Description**
At Simple Energy, we are dedicated to accelerating the world’s transition to sustainable mobility by creating high-performance, design-forward electric scooters. Our flagship products, Simple One and Simple Dot One, offer industry-leading range, advanced acceleration, generous storage, and futuristic aesthetics that prioritize both practicality and purpose. With features such as up to 248 km range, top speeds of 105 kmph, and zero-rejection manufacturing standards, we set high benchmarks for quality and innovation in the EV space. Our values center on going beyond expectations, pushing technological and design boundaries, and maintaining excellence through long-term reliability, including an 8-year motor warranty. Simple Energy is more than a scooter manufacturer—it is a movement reshaping how people experience and envision electric mobility.

**Role Description**
The SDE I – Android HMI App role is a full-time, on-site position based in Bengaluru. This role focuses on designing, developing, and maintaining Android-based Human Machine Interface (HMI) applications that power the user experience on Simple Energy’s electric scooters. Day-to-day responsibilities include implementing new features, optimizing performance, fixing bugs, and ensuring seamless integration between the Android app, vehicle systems, and backend services. The team member will collaborate closely with product managers, UI/UX designers, and hardware and firmware engineers to translate requirements into robust, user-friendly interfaces. The role also involves writing clean, maintainable code, participating in code reviews, and contributing to testing and documentation to ensure reliability and safety in real-world environments.

**What You'll Do**

* Develop and maintain HMI applications using Kotlin and modern Android development practices.
* Build reusable Jetpack Compose screens for dashboards, charging, vehicle controls, settings and notifications.
* Implement features within the existing architecture, following coding standards and production quality requirements.
* Integrate REST APIs, local settings and vehicle signals through established platform interfaces.
* Handle asynchronous updates using Coroutines and Flow, keeping UI state consistent with incoming data.
* Implement loading, error, offline and reconnection states, with appropriate guidance on vehicle-specific behavior.
* Support touch and joystick interactions, themes and feature availability across vehicle variants.
* Debug defects on HMI devices using ADB, Logcat and Android Studio; investigate logs and crash reports.
* Write unit and UI tests for assigned features and support QA during integration and release validation.
* Participate in code reviews and collaborate with design, platform, firmware, mobile, backend and QA teams.

**Required Skills**

* 1–3 years of professional Android application development experience.
* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Electronics or a related engineering discipline.
* Good proficiency in Kotlin, object-oriented programming and Jetpack Compose.
* Hands-on experience with Android SDK, Android Studio, application lifecycle, navigation and permissions.
* Understanding of MVVM or MVI, ViewModels, state management and separation of UI and business logic.
* Working knowledge of Kotlin Coroutines, Flow, StateFlow and asynchronous programming.
* Experience integrating REST APIs, parsing JSON and handling network errors.
* Understanding of local persistence and dependency injection; familiarity with DataStore and Koin or equivalent tools.
* Basic familiarity with CAN communication, vehicle signals or automotive system integration concepts.
* Experience with Git, branches, pull requests and collaborative development workflows.
* Strong debugging, analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work in an existing codebase.

**Good to Have**

* Exposure to Bluetooth/BLE, GATT or connected-device communication.
* Experience with GPS, maps or navigation SDKs such as Mappls.
* Familiarity with JUnit, Compose UI testing, Firebase Crashlytics or Android profiling tools.
* Exposure to Media3/ExoPlayer, Lottie, Java interoperability or custom Android system services.
* Basic knowledge of Gradle, build variants, application signing and secure data handling.

**What We're Looking For**

* Strong problem-solving and analytical ability.
* Good understanding of Android fundamentals beyond UI development.
* Ability to take ownership of assigned features and deliver them with appropriate engineering guidance.
* Ability to understand requirements and translate them into maintainable technical solutions.
* Willingness to participate actively in design discussions and code reviews.
* Ability to collaborate effectively with product, design, backend, QA, and other engineering teams.
* Curiosity to learn new technologies, platforms, and domain concepts.
* Focus on writing clean, maintainable, testable, and scalable code.

**Tech Stack**

**Core:**

Core: Kotlin • Jetpack Compose • Android SDK • MVVM • Coroutines • Flow • REST APIs • Git

**Supporting:**

Koin • Ktor • DataStore • CAN APIs • BLE • Mappls • Media3 • Firebase • JUnit • Gradle

What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that’s rare in established businesses.
  
  
The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we’ll give you the platform to define what comes next.
  
  
Join us at IG – the future gets built here.
  
  
**Your Team**
Join IG’s Prime Core team, which is responsible for building the open-spec trading APIs and solutions that support institutional and retail clients, delivering secure, high-performance, low-latency solutions.
  
  
**Your Role In The Team’s Success**
Our team sits within the IG Prime division, serving institutional and retail businesses. The Prime Core team owns the APIs that connect IG to institutional clients, brokers and partners across global markets — onboarding client accounts, funding, and the trading and market-data platform that our largest clients depend on every trading day.
  
  
That means real-time price distribution, order and execution flow, and reference data, running continuously through the trading day. When these systems degrade, clients notice immediately — so resilience, correctness and latency aren’t aspirations here; they’re the job. You’ll join at a genuinely interesting point: we’re building a new suite of cloud-native trading APIs.
  
  
**What You’ll Do**

* Write production Java that other people have to maintain: tested, readable, and honest about its edge cases.
* Work in a spec-driven, AI-assisted development workflow — specifying intent clearly, using AI tooling to move fast, and reviewing what comes back with a critical eye.
* Contribute to design discussions and technical decisions. You won’t be handed a spec and left alone; you’ll be in the room while we work out what to build.
* Deploy and run what you build in AWS, and learn how the cloud behaves when things go wrong.
* Investigate production issues alongside more experienced engineers — working from logs, metrics, traces and JVM diagnostics to get from symptom to root cause under time pressure.
* Grow into deeper ownership of services as you build confidence in the systems.

**What You’ll Need**

* Experience: 3–5 years of professional Java development experience, including hands-on AWS.
* Java: solid commercial experience writing Java in a production environment — this is the core of the role, and the thing we’ll dig into most.
* JVM: a real understanding of how the JVM behaves at runtime — memory management and garbage collection, the Java memory model, and how threads actually interact rather than how we hope they do.
* Concurrency and multi-threading: working knowledge, including the ways concurrent code fails: visibility problems, contention, and bugs that only appear under load.
* JVM diagnostics: practical skills reading thread and heap dumps, reasoning about GC behaviour, profiling, and narrowing down a memory leak or a contention problem rather than restarting and hoping.
* Spring: experience with the Spring Framework, ideally Spring Boot.
* AWS: hands-on experience — you’ve deployed and debugged something real in the cloud, and you understand the services you’ve used rather than just the commands you ran.
* AI coding tools: practical experience using them as part of your normal workflow, and the judgement to know when their output is wrong. We care much more about how critically you evaluate AI-generated code than how much of it you produce.
* Linux: comfort on Linux, including basic shell scripting.
* Curiosity: when something doesn’t add up, and the persistence to keep digging rather than working around it.
* Willingness to ask questions early and often. In a domain this specific, the engineers who learn fastest are the ones who ask.

**The Perks**
It really is more than a job. We think like a start-up, but we deliver like a FTSE 100 — so the bar is high, and we won’t pretend otherwise. We’ll recognise your talent and make sure that you can still have a life – at work, and outside of it. Networks, committees, awards, sports and social clubs, mentorships, volunteering opportunities, extra time off... the list goes on.
